newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Australia aims to double trade with Pakistan.
newsitem.headline: Australia aims to double trade with Pakistan.

text.p: Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Saturday he was confident that two-way trade between Australia and Pakistan would double in year 2000 from the existing 400 million Australian dollars.

"I feel confident that it will happen and I am confident that investment will also greatly expand," Fischer, who is also Trade Minister and heading a businessmen delegation to Pakistan, told a news conference in Islamabad.

Bilateral trade between the two countries stood at A$400 million in calender 1996. Australian exports to Pakistan were valued at A$260.5 million and imports from Pakistan were A$139.5 million, he said.
Australian investment in Pakistan was estimated at A$250 million and had a potential to expand to A$1.0 billion, he said.
Fischer said he was excited with the economic changes announced by the new government in Pakistan last week that would open more opportunities for trade and investment.
Pakistan slashed taxes and reduced maximum import tariffs to 45 percent from 65 percent effective July 1 under an economic reforms package unveiled by Finance Minister Sartaj Aziz.

He said he saw great potential for direct air links between Pakistan and Australia as trade partnership between the two countries was expected to grow in the future and urged airlines to move in to capture the niche market.
"I want to further facilitate air service links between Australia and Pakistan," Fischer said.
"As our partnership grows, we must have direct air links and not always through Singapore or Bangkok, which are now quite busy hubs.

"The first airline which moves down the path of offering Australia-Middle East direct service or Australia-Pakistan direct service will carve out a separate niche market, which I think will be quite lucrative," he added.
